decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'paste a link... click Fetch details... its basic details filled in automatically'; round 3 client: 'this quick-save flow works for me'. Round 6 recap: 'title and description are filled in for you'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url plus auto-fetch of title/description conforms to the reference; recorded conforming decision. (Favicon/preview-image capture from REF-BM-02 not clearly evidenced but not establishable as a divergence either.)

decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'the auto-filled title as editable after fetching (with a description shown for context)'; reinforced round 8 maker where the edit form is 'title, note, tags'. Round 3 client: 'Editing the fetched title is useful' — description editability not mentioned.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-03 requires editing the auto-collected title AND description before/after saving; the presentation makes description display-only (never appears in any edit surface). Client approved addressing only the title, so the difference passed without expression.

decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'tags so you type one and press Enter to add it as a removable chip' — no autocomplete offered; round 3 client: 'entering tags as removable chips feels natural' — autocomplete not mentioned.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-10 requires offering existing tags as autocomplete on entry; the presented chip-entry provides none. Client approved the chip mechanism without expressing the autocomplete expectation (contrast the rubric's example acceptance statement, which the client did not make).

decisions.evidence: round 3 maker: 'the note as an optional free-text line'; round 3 client: 'The optional note is also the right amount of effort for adding context' — no mention of markdown/rendering.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-23 (extended) requires a markdown note rendered when viewing; note is presented as plain free-text only. Approved without expressing the markdown difference.

decisions.evidence: round 4 maker pre-loads a readable list; round 7 'long' state shows title, note, and many tags on a card; round 3 shows description for context. Client accepts readability throughout.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title/description/tags conforms to REF-BM-07; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: round 4 maker: 'search to match across everything at once — a bookmark's title, its note, its link, and its tags' (description omitted from the enumeration); round 4 client: 'Broad search is what I'd expect, especially because I may remember a word from my note' — description not mentioned.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 requires full-text search over title, description, note, and url; the presented field set omits description (and adds tags, which is not judged one-way). Client endorsed 'broad' matching without surfacing the missing description field.

decisions.evidence: round 4 maker offered an either/or: 'having both feels right, or whether one alone would do'; round 4 client: 'Keeping clickable tag filters alongside search is useful too—I'd use either depending on what I remember.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Genuine alternatives differ in fulfilment: dropping click-to-filter chips would forgo REF-BM-11 (dropping search would forgo REF-BM-12). Offered decision marked diverged=true; client actively selected the reference-conforming option that preserves tag filtering — select.

decisions.evidence: round 5 maker: 'Read later as a toggle you can turn on or off at any time' with a separate Read later tab; round 5 client: 'Read later should be a reversible choice'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reversible read-later mark plus a separate unread list conforms to REF-BM-17/18/19. Client's restatement matches a conforming presentation, so no departure — not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: round 5 maker: 'Archive so archived links leave All and Read later entirely and live only in the Archive tab — still searchable there' with 'Restore to All'; round 5 client: 'archived links should disappear from the everyday views while remaining searchable and restorable in their own section.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive hides from default views, remains searchable, and is reversible/restorable (distinct from delete) — conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28.

decisions.evidence: round 7 maker offered: 'warn you it's a duplicate (and let you decide), or just save it again... I'd suggest warning you'; round 7 client: 'For a duplicate, please warn me and guide me to edit the existing bookmark rather than creating another copy.' Implemented in round 8 ('a button to edit the saved bookmark instead').
decisions.note: Specification gate. The maker's suggested default ('warn and let you decide') falls short of REF-BM-06's requirement to guide the user to edit the existing bookmark rather than create a new one; client supplied the reference-conforming behaviour explicitly — correct. Round-8 implementation is the linked disposition of this same decision, not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: round 8 maker offered an either/or: 'having that always-available Edit is welcome, or whether you'd rather editing only appear in the duplicate situation'; round 8 client: 'I'd also keep the Edit button available on every bookmark, since I may want to revise the title, note, or tags later'.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Alternatives differ in fulfilment: restricting Edit to the duplicate case would leave general bookmark editing (REF-BM-04) unfulfilled. Offered decision marked diverged=true; client selected the reference-conforming always-available Edit — select.

decisions.evidence: round 8 maker: 'the existing bookmark opens in the same form (title, note, tags)' — url and description absent from the edit form; round 8 client approved the edit/duplicate flow ('handles duplicates the way I wanted... update it') without noting missing url/description editing.
decisions.note: Implementation review. REF-BM-04 requires editing url/title/description/tags/note; the edit surface exposes only title, note, tags, so url (and description) editing is absent. The difference passed without a corrective response or explicit expression. Distinct from the description-at-save divergence (REF-BM-03) and from the always-available-Edit select above.
